results.finding: 1.2.3 hemiplegic migraine requires fully reversible motor weakness with visual, sensory or speech aura; 1.2.3.2 sporadic when no first- or second-degree relative is affected. 1.4.4 migraine aura-triggered seizure: a seizure during, or within 1 hour after, an attack of migraine with aura.
results.source: Headache Classification Committee of the IHS. ICHD-3. Cephalalgia 2018;38:1-211

results.finding: Combined hormonal methods are category 4 at any age in migraine with aura; progestogen-only methods and the copper IUD are category 1 or 2.
results.source: Faculty of Sexual and Reproductive Healthcare. UK Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use (UKMEC) 2016, amended 2019

results.finding: Topiramate must not be used for migraine prophylaxis in women of childbearing potential unless the conditions of the pregnancy prevention programme, including highly effective contraception, are met; it may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives.
results.source: MHRA Drug Safety Update, June 2024: topiramate pregnancy prevention programme

output.summary: ICHD-3 recognises seizures triggered by migraine aura; combined hormonal contraception is unacceptable in migraine with aura; topiramate needs a pregnancy prevention programme.

action_criteria.label: Take a structured headache and aura history with examination and red-flag review, applying ICHD-3 1.2.3 and 1.4.4
action_criteria.rationale: The history separates a prolonged hemiplegic aura with aura-triggered seizures from stroke, venous thrombosis and encephalitis, and identifies the red flags that need imaging and EEG.

action_criteria.label: Brain MRI: persistent deficit, reduced consciousness and first seizures during an attack
action_criteria.rationale: Required: a deficit lasting hours with seizures needs infarct, haemorrhage and other structural causes excluded.

action_criteria.rationale: Required: seizures with hemispheric cortical oedema in a woman taking combined oral contraception can be the presentation of cerebral venous thrombosis.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe triptans or ergot derivatives in hemiplegic migraine
Do not continue or start combined hormonal contraception (pill, patch or ring): migraine with aura is UKMEC category 4; offer an IUD or an implant, since topiramate weakens oral methods.
Do not offer valproate for migraine prevention or seizures in a woman who can become pregnant
required_recommendations: Diagnose a prolonged attack of sporadic hemiplegic migraine with migraine aura-triggered seizures (ICHD-3 1.2.3.2 and 1.4.4), with venous thrombosis, infarct and metabolic causes excluded
Stop Mercilon now: migraine with aura makes combined hormonal contraception UKMEC category 4

If topiramate is chosen, start it only with highly effective contraception (copper or hormonal IUD, or implant) under the topiramate pregnancy prevention programme; it reduces the efficacy of oral and progestogen-only pills

Review prevention, as she still has one to two attacks a month on topiramate 150 mg a day: continue topiramate under those conditions, or switch to lamotrigine (also treats seizures; levels rise once the pill is stopped) or verapamil
Treat attacks with an NSAID (for example naproxen 500 mg) and an antiemetic
Repeat brain MRI after recovery (for example at 4 to 6 weeks) to confirm the cortical changes have resolved; persistent change needs re-evaluation
Refer to clinical genetics for hemiplegic migraine gene testing (CACNA1A, ATP1A2, SCN1A, PRRT2)
Advise her not to drive and to tell the DVLA about the seizures if she holds a licence

avoided_actions.rationale: Once MRI is available a head CT adds nothing: MRI with diffusion answers infarct, haemorrhage and cortical oedema.
Echocardiography is not indicated: diffusion imaging shows no infarct and the lesion is not embolic.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated: the events were witnessed focal motor seizures, not syncope, and there is no infarct.

accepted: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine (ICHD-3 1.2.3) with migralepsy (single seizure during aura, ICHD-3 1.4.4) and reversible MRI changes — comprehensive workup excluded structural and metabolic mimics

differential.diagnosis: Familial hemiplegic migraine (CACNA1A, ATP1A2, SCN1A, PRRT2)
differential.key_features: Against: no first- or second-degree relative with similar attacks. A new pathogenic variant is still possible, hence the genetics referral.
Against: the seizures followed a visual aura and headache in a stereotyped attack type present since 14; no previous seizure; EEG without epileptiform discharges.
Against: MR venography shows patent sinuses and cortical veins; no haemorrhage on MRI.
Against: afebrile, CRP 2, recurrent stereotyped attacks with full recovery for 12 years, no subacute cognitive or psychiatric prodrome.
Against: lactate 1.3 mmol/L, previous mitochondrial blood tests normal, no hearing loss or short stature recorded, no maternal family history.
Against: no restricted diffusion after hours of deficit; cortical change crosses arterial territories.

Lactate and screening bloods normal; no family history of hemiplegic migraine

findings.result: Since age 14, one to two attacks a month of unilateral throbbing headache with arm weakness on alternating sides, always fully resolved within a few hours. Diagnosed as sporadic hemiplegic migraine at 22; normal CT, MRI, MRA, lumbar puncture and metabolic and mitochondrial blood tests at 17 and 22.

Blurred vision in the right visual field, then left-sided headache about 30 minutes later, then word-finding difficulty and right arm weakness after the headache peaked. Spread of each symptom over minutes not documented; no positive visual or sensory phenomena described.
Right-sided weakness and expressive dysphasia present for about 2 hours at assessment, within the 72-hour limit for motor aura; the visual field restriction is already improving.

During the speech and motor aura, within the hour after it began: two episodes of right-hand rhythmic jerking of about 90 seconds with unresponsiveness, followed by confusion for about 20 minutes. No previous seizure.
Fully reversible motor weakness with visual and speech aura in previous attacks (ICHD-3 1.2.3 B). No first- or second-degree relative with hemiplegic migraine (1.2.3.2 sporadic).

Topiramate 75 mg twice daily for two years, after flunarizine failed; still one to two attacks a month. Combined oral contraceptive Mercilon (ethinylestradiol 20 micrograms, desogestrel 150 micrograms).

GCS 14, temperature 37.1 C, BP 128/76. Expressive dysphasia, right homonymous field restriction (improving), right lower facial weakness, right arm power 3/5, right leg 4/5, right extensor plantar. Fundi normal.

Neurological deficit with impaired consciousness and first seizures: present. Hormonal contraception (oestrogen): present. Fever, sudden onset, onset after 50, pregnancy, positional trigger and papilloedema: absent.

clinical_assessment.impression: Prolonged attack of motor, visual and speech aura with headache in a woman with known sporadic hemiplegic migraine (ICHD-3 1.2.3.2; 4 of 6 criterion C characteristics in this attack), complicated by two focal seizures within an hour of the aura (fits ICHD-3 1.4.4 migraine aura-triggered seizure if no other cause is found). Red flags present: first seizures, impaired consciousness and use of an oestrogen-containing pill.

scores.ICHD-3 criterion C characteristics met (: 4 of 6 (succession, duration within the motor limit, unilateral, headache within 60 min)

alternatives: Contraception: copper IUD or levonorgestrel IUD (not affected by topiramate)
Prevention: lamotrigine (aura-predominant migraine; also an antiseizure medicine), verapamil, acetazolamide
Acute: NSAID (for example naproxen 500 mg) with an antiemetic
contraindications: Combined hormonal contraception in migraine with aura: UKMEC 2016 category 4 (unacceptable risk of ischaemic stroke); stop.
Triptans and ergot derivatives: avoid in hemiplegic migraine.
Valproate: not for migraine prevention in a woman who can become pregnant.
interactions: Topiramate + combined or progestogen-only pill: topiramate can reduce the contraceptive efficacy of oral hormonal methods (dose-related; MHRA 2024 advises not relying on them alone).
Lamotrigine + ethinylestradiol: oestrogen lowers lamotrigine levels by about half; levels rise when the pill is stopped.
Topiramate + acetazolamide: additive risk of metabolic acidosis and renal stones.
Verapamil + topiramate: no clinically relevant interaction.
Mercilon.proposed: Ethinylestradiol 20 micrograms with desogestrel 150 micrograms (Mercilon) and topiramate 75 mg twice daily in a 26-year-old woman with hemiplegic migraine and aura-triggered seizures
Mercilon.summary: Mercilon must stop (UKMEC 4 with aura); topiramate weakens oral contraception and needs the pregnancy prevention programme with an IUD; triptans, ergots and valproate are avoided.
warnings: Topiramate is teratogenic (oral clefts, low birth weight, possible neurodevelopmental effects); use requires the MHRA pregnancy prevention programme and highly effective contraception.
In migraine with aura the copper IUD is UKMEC category 1 and progestogen-only methods (levonorgestrel IUD, implant, desogestrel pill, injectable) are UKMEC category 2.

metadata.condition_name: Sporadic hemiplegic migraine with aura-triggered seizures and reversible cortical oedema, on a combined pill with topiramate
metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty due to MRI showing diffuse cortical swelling and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity (concerning for ischemia or encephalitis) with simultaneously normal DWI. Focal motor seizures complicate the picture (migralepsy consideration). Sporadic hemiplegic migraine diagnosis requires systematic exclusion of acute infarction, MELAS, epilepsy, and autoimmune causes.

patient.chief_complaint: Left-sided throbbing headache with right arm weakness, speech difficulty, and a witnessed shaking episode

family_history: No family history of hemiplegic migraine, stroke, or neurological disease. Mother has tension-type headache.

medications.indication: Migraine prevention; one to two attacks a month on treatment

social_history.note: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol (1-2 units/week), no illicit drugs. Lives with partner. Works as teaching assistant. Not pregnant.

patient.history_present_illness: A 26-year-old woman presented to the emergency department brought by her partner with a 3-hour history of severe left-sided throbbing headache that began approximately 30 minutes after she developed blurred vision in her right visual field. Shortly after the headache peaked, her partner noticed that she was struggling to find words and her right arm appeared weak. Within the following hour she experienced two brief episodes of right-hand rhythmic jerking lasting approximately 90 seconds each, during which she was unresponsive, followed by postictal confusion lasting approximately 20 minutes. She has had episodes of unilateral throbbing headache accompanied by transient arm weakness affecting alternating sides since the age of 14. During those earlier attacks, the weakness has always resolved completely within a few hours, and previous assessments including head CT, brain MRI, MR angiography, lumbar puncture, and basic metabolic and mitochondrial blood tests were all documented as normal at age 17 and again at age 22. She has not had a seizure before. She was commenced on topiramate 75 mg twice daily approximately two years ago following inadequate response to flunarizine; despite this she continues to have one to two attacks monthly. There is no family history of similar episodes, hemiplegic migraine, or any neurological condition. She does not smoke, drinks alcohol only occasionally, and uses no illicit substances. She takes topiramate and a combined oral contraceptive pill (Mercilon, desogestrel 150 mcg / ethinylestradiol 20 mcg). She has no known drug allergies.

neurological_exam.coordination: Limited on right due to weakness. Left cerebellar tests intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Visual fields by confrontation: mild right homonymous visual field restriction that patient reports is improving from earlier. Pupils 4mm equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full. Fundoscopy normal. Facial symmetry slightly reduced on right with right lower facial droop. Tongue protruded midline.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, mildly confused, oriented to person and place but not time. Motor aphasia: single-word responses, no paraphasic errors. Follows simple one-step commands.

neurological_exam.reflexes: Brisk throughout. Right plantar extensor (Babinski positive). Left plantar flexor.
neurological_exam.sensation: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. No cortical sensory deficits.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick bilaterally. No cortical sensory deficits.
